findings.summary: Successful platform-driver registration is not undone on later init failures or normal module cleanup.
evidence: Stock init assembly registers the driver with __this_module at section offset 0x80 before alloc_chrdev_region at 0xa8.
Stock init error edges after a successful registration do not call platform_driver_unregister.
Stock cleanup_module has no platform_driver_unregister call.
Pinned bus_add_driver adds the driver to the bus list and calls driver_attach; platform_driver_unregister removes it through driver_unregister and bus_remove_driver.
Pinned do_init_module failure path frees the module without invoking its exit callback.
findings.interpretation: A registration may remain on the platform bus while callback or driver storage is released. This is a static lifetime hazard and potential stale callback reference; runtime use-after-free was not reproduced.

findings.summary: cleanup_module requests release of one character-device minor although init reserved a range of 16.
evidence: Init passes g_rdbg_instance.count, initialized to 16, to alloc_chrdev_region.
Stock cleanup assembly passes count 1 to unregister_chrdev_region.
Pinned __unregister_chrdev_region requires the stored minorct to equal the requested count, so the count-1 call does not remove the count-16 range.
findings.interpretation: The device-number range remains reserved after cleanup. This is statically established from the pinned implementation; no runtime reload test was run.

findings.summary: A failed platform_driver_register return leaves the previously allocated clients array unfreed.
evidence: Init allocates 16 client entries of stride 0x1c8, then returns ret directly when platform_driver_register fails.
The failed driver-core registration path unwinds its own partial bus registration, but the separate clients allocation has no kfree on this edge.
findings.interpretation: A 7296-byte allocation can leak when platform-driver registration fails.

reconstruction_disposition: All three behaviors are stock-matching; no source or map change was made. Keep the eight offline-exact mapping statuses, but do not describe rdbg as runtime-safe or fully validated.
